verdict.line: You lose if you let him hit max Rage and dive you at full HP; you win every trade he takes without it.

brief.thesis: Teemo vs Gnar is dead even on the numbers (54.2% over 1433 games) because both champions are poke-based ranged laners fighting for the same space at 680/1100 range. The lane is decided by who manages Gnar's Rage Gene and who controls Blinding Dart's 8-second cooldown, not by raw stats.

theirWindow.what: He is about to transform into Mega Gnar on his next ability use, which removes his ranged Boomerang Throw poke and gives him a melee W (Wallop) stun and E (Crunch) AoE. Do not stand still in his face at full Rage — back off to 680+ range and reset the fight on your terms.

yourWindow.when: his Q (Boomerang Throw) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With no boomerang in hand, Gnar has no poke tool until it returns or recharges (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s). Walk up and land Toxic Shot autos or a Blinding Dart to blind him before he can punish the approach.

powerCurve.note: both poking at range, no transform yet
mini-Gnar Rage procs enable quick all-ins
Toxic Shot stacks offset his hyper damage

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: 55.7% win rate over 1387 games (76% pick rate) — the extra sustain and mana regen let you hold Blinding Dart for trades instead of auto-poking alone.

boots.why: 54% win rate over 774 games (44.4% pick) — magic penetration scales your Toxic Shot and Liandry's damage through his armor stacking.

core.why: attack speed plus the proc punishes him for standing in poke range to land his own Boomerang Throw
burn stacks compound with Toxic Shot's damage-over-time for a 58% win rate over 522 games on this path
ability haste drops your Blinding Dart cooldown further, letting you blind him more often during his all-in windows

situational.when: he builds any magic resist to answer your DoT damage
you are ahead and want to snowball attack speed for faster Toxic Shot stacking
the game goes long and you need to one-shot squishies with mushrooms

runes.keystoneWhy: rewards sustained autos in extended poke trades and punishes Gnar for staying in range to fight back

summoners.why: run at 54.7% win rate and 93.5% pick rate — Ignite closes out poke trades before he can transform and disengage, Flash dodges his E (Hop) engage.

playing.title: Track Rage before every trade
playing.detail: Check his Rage bar before committing to an auto exchange. At max Rage his next ability flips him into Mega Gnar with a melee stun — disengage to range instead of continuing the trade.

playing.title: Hold Blinding Dart for his engage
playing.detail: Blinding Dart has an 8-second cooldown and blinds him on a 680-range hit — save it to shut down his transformed W (Wallop) stun attempt or his E (Hop) landing, not just for chip damage.

playing.title: Poke when his Q is down
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw's cooldown is 16 down to 10 seconds with rank; once he's thrown it and missed the catch, close distance and stack Toxic Shot autos freely.

playing.title: Use Camouflage to reset trades
playing.detail: Stand still after a trade to go Invisible, then re-engage with the Element of Surprise attack speed buff when he's expecting disengage.

playing.title: Respect the mega form's E (Crunch)
playing.detail: Once transformed, his E deals AoE damage around his landing spot instead of bouncing off a unit — don't stand near where he lands even if you dodged the initial hit.

playing.title: Place mushrooms on his jungle entrances
playing.detail: Noxious Trap has only a 1-second cooldown between plants — pre-seed river and tri-brush so his all-in or gank attempts walk into a slow and DoT before he reaches you.

playing.title: Punish post-transform cooldowns
playing.detail: After he reverts from Mega Gnar his mobility and stun are gone for a stretch — this is your highest-value window to shove the wave or force a kill with Ignite up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the Rage-tracking and cooldown-window tactics are my own reading of the mechanics, not measured data.
